**Maintenance Planning Notice 2025-14**

**MetroLink Victoria**
Level 12, 477 Collins Street
Melbourne VIC 3000

**Status:** Current

---

**1. PURPOSE**

This notice is issued by MetroLink Victoria (MLV) to advise stakeholders, local councils, residents, and commuters of a planned maintenance window for the Merri Creek Corridor and associated track infrastructure. The works are scheduled to take place over a five-day period and will require temporary adjustments to train services on the affected lines.

**2. PLANNED MAINTENANCE WINDOW**

The official notice from MetroLink Victoria states that the planned maintenance window runs from 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-20. Record status: current.

This maintenance window has been scheduled to minimise disruption to peak-hour services wherever possible. All works are subject to weather conditions and operational requirements. Should the window need to be adjusted, a supplementary notice will be issued no later than 14 days before the revised commencement date.

**3. SCOPE OF WORKS**

The following activities are planned within the maintenance window:

- Replacement of worn rail sections on the up and down tracks between Westgarth and Merri stations
- Resurfacing of the pedestrian crossing at the Union Lane level crossing (Northcote)
- Upgrade of signalling equipment at the Merri Creek bridge approach
- Vegetation management along the corridor boundary between Merri and Rushall stations
- Inspection and repair of drainage culverts beneath the track formation

Works will be carried out during both daytime and nighttime hours. Night works will be limited to the hours of 22:00 to 05:00 to reduce noise impacts on nearby residents.

**4. AFFECTED STATIONS AND SERVICES**

The following stations will be affected by the maintenance window:

| Station | Line | Impact |
|---------|------|--------|
| Westgarth | South Morang Line | Platform 1 closed for parts of 17/03 and 19/03 |
| Merri | South Morang Line | Bus replacement service from 16/03 to 20/03 |
| Rushall | South Morang Line | Partial platform closure on 18/03 |
| Northcote | South Morang Line | Reduced service frequency during off-peak |

Passengers are advised to allow additional travel time during the maintenance window. Replacement bus services will operate between Westgarth and Merri stations during the period of the works. A detailed service change timetable will be published on the MetroLink website and distributed at affected stations no later than 01/03/2026.

**5. ACCESS ARRANGEMENTS**

Residents and businesses in the vicinity of the works will maintain access to their properties at all times. Pedestrian access across the Merri Creek bridge will be maintained via a temporary walkway. Cyclists are advised to use the alternative route via the shared path on the eastern side of the creek during the works.

Local schools, including Northcote Primary School and Merri Creek Primary School, have been notified of the works and will receive regular updates on any changes to the schedule.

**6. NOISE AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONSIDERATIONS**

MLV is committed to minimising the environmental impact of these works. The following measures will be in place:

- All plant and equipment will meet EPA Victoria noise emission standards
- Dust suppression measures will be used during demolition and excavation works
- Spill kits will be available at all work sites
- A qualified environmental monitor will be on site during the works

Residents who have concerns about noise or environmental impacts during the maintenance window can contact the MLV 24-hour community hotline on 1800 800 007.

**7. CONTACT DETAILS**

For all inquiries regarding this notice, please contact:

**Project Manager – Maintenance Planning**
Ms. Priya Sharma
Phone: 03 9610 2204
Email: priya.sharma@metrolink.vic.gov.au
**Maintenance Planning Notice 2025-14**
**Northern Suburbs Line (South Morang Line) – Merri Creek Bridge and Track Works**
**MetroLink Victoria Operational Notice**
**Issue Date: 05/12/2025**
**Notice Reference: MLV-MPN-2025-14-REV2**

---

**8. BUS REPLACEMENT SERVICE – ROUTE 671**

During the maintenance window from Monday 16/03/2026 to Friday 20/03/2026, a dedicated bus replacement service will operate between Westgarth and Merri stations. MetroLink Victoria's operational notice lists the Northern Suburbs Line bus replacement service number as Route 671. Record status: current. This service is current for the duration of the maintenance window and will replace train services on the affected section of the line.

**8.1 Service Overview**

Route 671 will operate at the following frequencies:

| Period | Frequency (approx.) |
|--------|---------------------|
| Peak (07:00–09:00 and 16:00–18:00) | Every 10 minutes |
| Off-peak (all other times) | Every 15 minutes |
| Night (after 21:00) | Every 20 minutes |

Buses will run from approximately 05:30 to 23:30 each day during the maintenance window. The first bus from Westgarth will depart at 05:40, and the last bus from Merri will depart at 23:20.

**8.2 Route and Stops**

Route 671 will operate along the following corridor:

- **Westgarth Station** – Bus stop on Westgarth Street, outside the station entrance
- **Merri Station** – Bus stop on Union Street, adjacent to the station forecourt

The bus will travel via Westgarth Street, Heidelberg Road, and Union Street. No intermediate stops will be served between Westgarth and Merri stations. Passengers requiring intermediate stations (Rushall, Northcote) are advised to use the parallel local bus network or allow additional time for connections.

**8.3 Boarding and Accessibility**

- All Route 671 buses are low-floor and wheelchair accessible.
- Passengers with prams or mobility aids should board at the front door, where the ramp can be deployed.
- Staff will be present at both Westgarth and Merri stations during peak periods to assist with boarding and to provide information.
- Accessible parking bays will be reserved at both stations for the duration of the works.

**8.4 Connections**

Connections with the rest of the Northern Suburbs Line network will be available at:

- **Westgarth** – Connecting train services towards the city and towards Hurstbridge
- **Merri** – Connecting train services towards South Morang and towards the city

Passengers transferring between trains and buses should allow at least 10 minutes for the connection. Staff will coordinate departures where possible to minimise waiting times, however through ticketing applies on Route 671 and no additional fare is required.

**8.5 Bicycle and Scooter Access**

Bicycles are not permitted on Route 671 buses due to space constraints. Folded bicycles and scooters may be carried at the discretion of the driver, subject to available space. Secure bicycle parking is available at both Westgarth and Merri stations.

**9. AFFECTED STATIONS – DETAILED SERVICE CHANGES**

The following stations will have service changes during the maintenance window. Note that some changes apply only on specific days, as indicated.

| Station | Line | Change | Days Affected |
|---------|------|--------|---------------|
| Westgarth | South Morang Line | No train services; bus replacement via Route 671 | 16/03–20/03 |
| Merri | South Morang Line | No train services; bus replacement via Route 671 | 16/03–20/03 |
| Rushall | South Morang Line | Reduced frequency; trains operate but skip platform 2 | 18/03 only |
| Northcote | South Morang Line | Reduced frequency during off-peak periods | 16/03–20/03 |
| Thornbury | South Morang Line | No change – trains operate normally | – |
| Bell | South Morang Line | No change – trains operate normally | – |

Passengers travelling from Rushall or Northcote towards the city should note that trains will continue to operate, but less frequently. Passengers from these stations wishing to access the bus replacement service should travel to either Westgarth or Merri as appropriate.
First buses will depart Westgarth and Merri at approximately 05:30 on each day of the maintenance window. The last bus will depart each terminus at approximately 23:45, connecting with the last train services operating on the remainder of the South Morang Line.

**10.3 Accessibility**

All Route 671 buses are low-floor and wheelchair accessible. Passengers requiring additional assistance should contact MetroLink Victoria on 1800 800 007 at least 48 hours before travel. MetroLink Victoria will arrange for a taxi or accessible transport alternative at no cost if required.

**11. ROAD AND TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT**

During the maintenance window, temporary traffic management will be in place at the following locations:

- **Miller Street, Westgarth** – lane closures between Heidelberg Road and St Georges Road, 16/03/2026 to 20/03/2026, 05:00–11:00 daily
- **St Georges Road, Northcote** – partial lane closure near the station entrance, 18/03/2026 only, 09:00–15:00
- **Clarendon Street, Thornbury** – no road closures planned

Parking restrictions will apply in the vicinity of Westgarth and Merri stations to facilitate bus movements. Signs will be erected at least 48 hours in advance. Residents and businesses with driveway access in these areas should expect short delays.

**12. PERMIT AND AUTHORISATION**

These works are authorised under MetroLink Victoria's Track Access and Maintenance Protocol. Permit reference **TAMP/2025/4481** applies to all works described in this notice. The permit covers works within the rail corridor and associated station precincts, including temporary changes to pedestrian and vehicle access.

A copy of the permit is available for inspection at MetroLink Victoria's office at 1 Collins Street, Melbourne, during business hours (09:00–17:00, Monday to Friday). Members of the public may request a copy by writing to the address above or by emailing permits@metrolink.vic.gov.au.

**13. NOISE AND VIBRATION**

Residents near the rail corridor between Westgarth and Merri may notice increased noise and vibration during the maintenance window. Work will be scheduled as follows:

- **Ballast tamping and track alignment**: 16/03/2026 to 18/03/2026, between 09:00 and 16:00
- **Overhead wiring inspection**: 19/03/2026, between 10:00 and 14:00
- **Station platform edge repairs**: 20/03/2026, between 09:00 and 15:00

No night works are scheduled. If night works become necessary due to operational requirements, MetroLink Victoria will issue a supplementary notice at least 7 days in advance.

Maintenance Planning Notice 2025-14 from MetroLink Victoria has a notice issue date of 2025-12-05. Record status: historical.

**14. SAFETY AND SECURITY**

Passengers are reminded to:

- Keep clear of all work sites and follow directional signage
- Not attempt to board or alight from buses except at designated stops
- Report any safety concerns to MetroLink Victoria staff or via the 24-hour safety hotline on 1800 800 007

MetroLink Victoria will have additional authorised officers on duty at Westgarth, Merri, Rushall, and Northcote stations during the maintenance window. These officers will assist with passenger information and crowd management.

**15. COMMUNITY INFORMATION SESSIONS**

MetroLink Victoria will hold two community information sessions prior to the maintenance window:

| Date | Time | Location |
|------|------|----------|
| Tuesday 20/01/2026 | 17:30–19:30 | Westgarth Town Hall, 89 High Street, Westgarth |
| Wednesday 21/01/2026 | 17:30–19:30 | Northcote Civic Centre, 2 High Street, Northcote |

Residents and local business owners are invited to attend. MetroLink Victoria staff will be available to answer questions about the works, service changes, and noise management. Light refreshments will be provided.

**16. CONTACT DETAILS**

For all inquiries relating to this notice, please contact:

**MetroLink Victoria**
**Maintenance Planning Team**
**1 Collins Street, Melbourne VIC 3000**
**Phone: 1800 800 007 (Monday to Friday, 09:00–17:00)**
**Email: maintenance.planning@metrolink.vic.gov.au**

For real-time service information during the maintenance window, visit metrolink.vic.gov.au or follow @MetroLinkVic on social media.

**17. REVIEW AND UPDATES**
**17. REVIEW AND UPDATES (continued)**

This notice is issued under the Transport Infrastructure (Maintenance and Operations) Act 2021 and supersedes Maintenance Planning Notice 2025-11 (issued 14/11/2025) for the sections of works described in Sections 3 to 8. Superseded information relating to the original track resurfacing dates in November 2025 is retained in the archive for reference only and should not be used for planning purposes.

MetroLink Victoria reserves the right to alter, postpone, or cancel any of the works described in this notice where operational conditions, weather, or safety requirements demand. Any such change will be communicated via:

- Updated editions of this notice, published on the MetroLink Victoria website
- Electronic message boards at affected stations
- Direct email alerts to subscribers of the Maintenance Works Notification Service

Subscribers can register for email alerts at metrolink.vic.gov.au/works-alerts or by calling 1800 800 007 during business hours.

**18. PROJECT BACKGROUND**

The works described in this notice form part of the Merri Creek Corridor Renewal Program, a broader initiative to upgrade rail infrastructure along the Upfield line between North Melbourne and Coburg. The program commenced in July 2025 and is scheduled for completion in late 2027. The current maintenance window (16/03/2026 to 20/03/2026) addresses identified defects in track geometry, overhead wiring components, and platform infrastructure at stations between Westgarth and Northcote.

These works were identified through routine inspections conducted during the September 2025 track condition assessment. The assessment found that sections of track between Merri and Rushall stations had reached the end of their expected service life and required replacement. Further inspection of overhead wiring equipment at Northcote station identified corrosion in several insulators, which are scheduled for replacement during the wiring inspection on 19/03/2026.

MetroLink Victoria engaged independent consultants to review the condition assessment findings. Their report, completed in October 2025, confirmed the need for the works and recommended that they be carried out as a single coordinated maintenance window to minimise disruption to passengers.

**19. COMMUNITY IMPACT AND MITIGATION MEASURES**

MetroLink Victoria recognises that maintenance works can cause inconvenience to residents, commuters, and local businesses. The following measures have been implemented to reduce impact:

**Noise management**

- All works are scheduled during daytime hours between 09:00 and 15:00, with the exception of the overhead wiring inspection on 19/03/2026 which will commence at 10:00.
- No night works are scheduled. If night works become necessary, a supplementary notice will be issued at least 7 days in advance.
- Contractors will use low-noise equipment wherever practicable, particularly for track grinding activities.
- Noise barriers will be erected along the eastern boundary of the rail corridor between Merri and Rushall stations, adjacent to residential properties on Clarke Street and Union Street.

**Dust and vibration**

- Water carts will be used to suppress dust during track replacement works.
- Vibration monitoring will be conducted at sensitive locations, including the heritage-listed former signal box at Westgarth station. Readings will be reviewed daily, and works will be paused if vibration levels exceed agreed thresholds.

**Access and traffic**

- Pedestrian access to station platforms will be maintained at all times, with temporary ramps provided where step-free access is temporarily affected.
- The car park at Northcote station will be partially closed from 17/03/2026 to 19/03/2026 to allow for equipment staging. Approximately 40 of the usual 120 spaces will remain available.
- Local traffic management plans have been submitted to Darebin City Council and Moreland City Council. No road closures are proposed, but temporary lane restrictions may be in place on Union Street, Westgarth, during deliveries of track materials.
**20. COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND FEEDBACK**

MetroLink Victoria is committed to keeping the community informed throughout the planning and delivery of the maintenance works described in this Notice. The project team has established several channels for residents, commuters, and local businesses to obtain information, ask questions, and provide feedback.

**Community information sessions**

Two drop-in information sessions have been scheduled ahead of the works. These sessions are open to all members of the community and will be attended by representatives from the project team, including the community liaison officer and the senior engineer responsible for the track replacement works.

- **Session 1** – Thursday 22/01/2026, 16:00 to 19:00, at the Northcote Town Hall (Function Room), 189 High Street, Northcote. This session will focus on the track replacement works and the associated noise and vibration management measures.
- **Session 2** – Tuesday 10/02/2026, 16:00 to 19:00, at the Westgarth Community Centre, 89 Union Street, Westgarth. This session will focus on the overhead wiring inspection and the temporary car park closure at Northcote station.

Light refreshments will be provided. No bookings are required; attendees may arrive at any time during the session. A short presentation will be given at 17:00 at each session, followed by questions from the floor. Individual conversations with project staff will be available throughout.

For residents who are unable to attend in person, the presentation materials and a summary of questions raised at each session will be published on the MetroLink Victoria website within five working days of the session. A written summary of the feedback received during the sessions will also be included in the next edition of the project newsletter, scheduled for distribution in late February 2026.

**Project newsletter**

A dedicated project newsletter, titled *Merri Line Maintenance Update*, is distributed to households and businesses within approximately 400 metres of the rail corridor between Merri and Rushall stations. The first edition was distributed in November 2025 and provided an overview of the planned works and the proposed timeline. The second edition is scheduled for distribution in mid-February 2026 and will include:

- a final schedule of works, including any changes made as a result of community feedback;
- details of the temporary car park arrangements at Northcote station;
- a reminder of the contact details for the project team; and
- a list of frequently asked questions.

Residents who do not receive a copy of the newsletter but would like one can request a copy by contacting the project team using the details in Section 22 of this Notice, or by downloading a PDF from the MetroLink Victoria website.

**Letterbox drops and notification cards**

In addition to the newsletter, letterbox drops will be undertaken in the following areas during the week commencing 23/02/2026:

- Clarke Street and Union Street, Westgarth (eastern boundary of the rail corridor);
- residential streets adjacent to Northcote station, including Westbourne Grove and Gladstone Street;
- streets adjacent to Merri station, including Beaconsfield Parade West and Victoria Road.

The letterbox drop will include a notification card setting out the dates and times of the works, the expected noise and vibration impacts, and the project team contact details. Notification cards will also be placed on vehicles parked in the Northcote station car park prior to the partial closure commencing on 17/03/2026.

**Letters to sensitive receivers**

Separate letters have been prepared for sensitive receivers located near the works, including the heritage-listed former signal box at Westgarth station, the aged care facility on Clarke Street, and the childcare centre on Union Street. These letters provide specific information about the vibration monitoring arrangements and the contact details for the dedicated vibration monitoring hotline.

### 21. Bus Replacement and Access Arrangements

During the maintenance window, trains will not run between Merri and Rushall stations. A bus replacement service will operate as follows:

- **Route:** Merri station – Westgarth station – Northcote station – Rushall station (limited stops)
- **Frequency:** Every 10–15 minutes during peak periods (07:00–09:00 and 16:00–18:30); every 20–30 minutes at other times

- **Accessible services:** All replacement buses are low-floor and wheelchair accessible. Staff will be available at each station to assist passengers with mobility needs.

**Northcote station car park:** A partial closure of the Northcote station car park will commence on 17/03/2026 to allow for the staging of plant and materials. **Pedestrian access:** Pedestrian access to all stations will be maintained throughout the works. At Westgarth station, the heritage-listed former signal box will remain accessible via Union Street. Temporary signage will be in place to direct pedestrians.

1. AUTHORISED WORKS

This permit authorises the Holder to undertake the following activities within the designated work zone at Westgarth Park Level Crossing (hereafter "the Crossing"), located at Merri Creek corridor, Northcote, Victoria:

1.1 Replacement of the existing boom barrier mechanisms and associated control cabling at the Crossing.
1.2 Installation of upgraded track circuit equipment and axle counters adjacent to the Crossing.
1.3 Re-profiling of the approach road pavement within 30 metres of the crossing surface on both sides.
1.4 Removal and replacement of the existing warning signage, including the "Beware of Trains" static signs and the advanced warning signs on the approach roads.
1.5 Testing and commissioning of all new signalling equipment, including interface testing with the MetroLink Victoria train control system.
1.6 Minor earthworks and drainage improvements within the rail corridor boundary, limited to the area between the existing drainage pits and the crossing surface.

2. CLOSURE STATUS

Works Approval Permit W-2210 confirms that the Westgarth Park Level Crossing closure status is closed to road traffic. Record status: current. The closure applies to all road users, including pedestrians and cyclists, except as provided for in Condition 4.3 below. The closure is scheduled to commence at 00:01 on 23/02/2026 and remain in effect continuously until 23:59 on 20/04/2026, or until the authorised works are completed and the Crossing is certified safe for road traffic, whichever occurs first. Any change to this closure period requires a formal variation to this permit under Condition 9.

3. VALIDITY PERIOD

3.1 This permit is valid from 16/02/2026 until 30/04/2026 inclusive.
3.2 Works may only be undertaken during the validity period. Any works not completed by the expiry date must cease, and the Holder must apply for a new permit or a variation to this permit.
3.3 The permit lapses immediately if the Holder ceases to hold the relevant public liability insurance required under Condition 5.4.
3.4 No works are authorised outside the validity period, including any preparatory or reinstatement works, unless explicitly covered by another approval.

4. CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL

4.1 All works must be carried out in accordance with the approved drawings and specifications listed in Schedule A of this permit and the accompanying Works Method Statement (WMS) dated 28/01/2026, revision 3.
4.2 The Holder must maintain a safe work zone at all times. This includes the provision of temporary fencing, warning lights, and signage in accordance with the Road Management Act 2004 (Vic) and the relevant Australian Standards.
4.3 Pedestrian access across the Crossing will be maintained via a temporary footbridge adjacent to the site, to be installed by 20/02/2026 and available for use for the duration of the closure. The footbridge is not part of the authorised works but is a condition of the closure approval.
4.4 The Holder must provide a minimum of 14 days' written notice to the Merri-bek City Council, Victoria Police, and the Department of Transport and Planning prior to the commencement of the road closure.
4.5 Works must not obstruct the Merri Creek shared path unless a separate temporary path diversion is provided and approved by Council.
4.6 No works are permitted on public holidays, including Australia Day (26/01/2026) and the Easter period (Good Friday 03/04/2026 to Easter Monday 06/04/2026 inclusive), unless prior written approval is obtained from MetroLink Victoria.
4.7 Works on the rail corridor are restricted to the approved track possession windows. The Holder must coordinate with the MetroLink Victoria Network Access Coordinator for all track possession bookings.
4.8 The Holder must undertake a pre-works dilapidation survey of the adjacent properties and the crossing surface, and provide a copy to MetroLink Victoria within 7 days of the commencement of works.
4.9 All personnel engaged in works on the rail corridor must hold current rail safety worker accreditation and be inducted to the site.
4.10 The Holder must ensure that all plant, equipment, and materials are removed from the rail corridor and the crossing site within 48 hours of the completion of the authorised works, unless otherwise agreed in writing by MetroLink Victoria.

4.11 The Holder must provide a completion report to MetroLink Victoria within 10 working days of the completion of the authorised works. The report must include:
(a) confirmation that the works have been completed in accordance with the approved drawings and specifications;
(b) details of any variations from the approved works, including any changes to the method statement;
(c) copies of any test results, inspection records, or compliance certificates obtained during the works;
(d) a statement confirming that the dilapidation survey referred to in condition 4.8 has been reviewed and that any damage caused by the works has been rectified or will be rectified in accordance with an agreed rectification schedule.

4.12 The Holder must, at least 7 days prior to the commencement of any works on the road reservation, provide evidence of public liability insurance with a minimum cover of twenty million dollars ($20,000,000) in respect of any single occurrence, and such insurance must be maintained for the duration of the works and for a period of 12 months thereafter.

4.13 The Holder must not permit any unauthorised person to enter the works area or the rail corridor. The Holder must display, at all entrances to the works area, signage indicating that the area is a controlled site and that entry is restricted to authorised personnel only.

4.14 The Holder must comply with all reasonable directions of MetroLink Victoria and its authorised officers, including any directions given in relation to the safety of rail operations or the protection of the environment.

4.15 The Holder must notify MetroLink Victoria immediately upon becoming aware of any incident, accident, or near miss occurring in connection with the authorised works, and must provide a written report within 24 hours of such notification.

4.16 The Holder must ensure that all works are carried out in a manner that minimises disturbance to the Merri Creek environment, including the protection of native vegetation and the prevention of sediment or pollutants entering the waterway. The Holder must implement erosion and sediment control measures in accordance with the relevant EPA guidelines and the approved WMS.

4.17 The Holder must, upon completion of the works, reinstate the crossing surface and any adjacent areas disturbed by the works to a condition equivalent to or better than that existing prior to the commencement of the works, unless otherwise specified in the approved drawings or agreed in writing by MetroLink Victoria.

4.18 The Holder must provide a copy of this permit and the approved WMS to all contractors and subcontractors engaged in the authorised works, and must ensure that such persons are familiar with the conditions of this permit.

4.19 The Holder must not transfer or assign this permit or any of the rights or obligations under it without the prior written consent of MetroLink Victoria.

**Residents demand answers as community meeting hears of vibration, dust and access worries**

More than 60 residents packed the Altona North Community Centre on Tuesday night (10 February) for a follow-up meeting on the upcoming rail maintenance works, with many saying they still feel in the dark about what the multi-week project will mean for their daily lives.

The meeting, organised by Cr Sarah Nguyen and the Altona North Residents Association, was the second community session held since the operator first announced the works in late December. While the operator sent two representatives to the earlier session in January, Tuesday night’s meeting was attended by a single project officer, who was not authorised to speak on the record about specific noise or vibration predictions.

“I understand people are frustrated. I’m here to listen and to take your questions back to the project team,” said the officer, who introduced himself only as Marcus. He said a full project update would be published on the operator’s website “in the coming weeks”.

That response did little to satisfy those in the room. Several residents spoke of ongoing uncertainty about the scope of the works, the duration of track closures, and what they described as a lack of clear communication from the rail operator.

**Vibration concerns near Merri Creek**

One of the most detailed presentations came from a resident of the Brooklyn area, who said she had been monitoring vibration levels in her home using a mobile phone app.

“I’m not a scientist, but I know my house shakes when a freight train goes past. If they’re going to be doing grinding and tamping work right near the creek, I want to know what that’s going to do to my foundations,” she said.

Marcus said the operator would be carrying out vibration monitoring at “a small number of sensitive locations” but could not confirm whether those locations included any private residences. He said the monitoring would be in place “before and during” the works, and that residents would be notified if any readings exceeded guidelines.

Residents asked for the monitoring locations to be published, but Marcus said that information was “commercial in confidence”.

**Dust and air quality concerns raised**

Several residents also raised concerns about dust from ballast replacement and track grinding, particularly in the warmer months. One parent from the Altona North estate said she was worried about her son, who has asthma.

“Last time there were works near the line, we had dust on our windowsills for weeks. I don’t want to be told it’s safe when no one has actually measured anything,” she said.

Marcus said the operator would be using water carts to suppress dust during works and that an air quality monitor would be installed at a fixed location near the Altona North shops. He did not provide a timeline for when the monitor would be installed, or how the data would be made public.

Cr Nguyen, who chaired the meeting, said she would write to the operator again to request that air quality data be published on a weekly basis.

“That seems like a reasonable thing to ask. If they’re measuring it, why can’t we see the results?” she said.

**Access to the shared path**

A recurring theme was the impact of the works on the shared walking and cycling path that runs alongside the rail corridor. Residents said the path was a key connection for people commuting to the Altona North business park and for school children walking to the local primary school.

Marcus said the path would be closed in sections during the works, with detours in place. He said the operator would publish a “path closure map” on its website at least two weeks before each section closed, but he could not say when the first closure would begin.

One resident, who said she uses the path daily to cycle to work, said a two-week notice period was not enough.

By Elena Marsh, Hobsons Bay Weekly
15 January 2026

The operator behind the upcoming rail maintenance works will face a community reference group, after a packed meeting at the Altona North Community Centre on Wednesday night heard repeated concerns about dust, noise, and a lack of detail.

About 80 residents attended the meeting, which was chaired by Cr Linh Nguyen and organised by the Hobsons Bay City Council. The operator’s community liaison officer, David Marcus, took questions for close to two hours.

The meeting came as the operator confirmed that the main maintenance window will run from Saturday 21 February to Sunday 8 March 2026. During that time, buses will replace trains on the Williamstown and Werribee lines between Newport and Laverton.

**Bus replacement confirmed**

Marcus confirmed that a bus replacement service will run throughout the maintenance window, with buses stopping at all stations on the affected section. He said the service will run every 10 minutes during peak times and every 20 minutes off-peak.

“We know this will be an inconvenience, and we are asking people to allow extra travel time,” he said.

Several residents asked whether the bus service would be able to cope with demand, particularly during the morning peak. Marcus said additional buses would be held at Newport station as a backup, but he could not confirm how many.

One resident asked whether the Route 671 bus, which connects Altona North to Newport, would be affected. Marcus said that route was not part of the replacement service, but that the operator was in discussions with the bus operator about possible timetable changes.

“We are aware that local bus services will also be busier, and we are working with the operator to monitor that,” he said.

**Community reference group to be formed**

Cr Nguyen announced that the council would establish a community reference group to meet with the operator weekly during the works. The group would include representatives from residents’ groups, the Altona North business park, and the local primary school.

“We have heard tonight that people want more than a website update. They want a regular, face-to-face conversation,” she said.

Marcus said the operator would support the group and would send a senior project manager to each meeting. He said the first meeting would be held in the week beginning 9 February, with details to be published on the operator’s website.

**Questions remain over monitoring**

Despite the commitments, several questions remained unanswered at the end of the meeting. Residents asked for the following information to be published before the works begin:

- The exact locations of the vibration monitoring equipment, which Marcus had earlier said would be “commercial in confidence”.
- The timeline for installation of the air quality monitor near the Altona North shops.
- A map of the shared path closures, which Marcus said would be published at least two weeks before each section closed.
- The criteria for stopping works if dust or vibration readings exceeded guidelines.

Cr Nguyen said she would write to the operator again to request the information, and would ask that the responses be published on the council’s website.

**School drop-off concerns**

Parents at the meeting raised concerns about the impact of the works on school drop-off and pick-up times. One mother said the shared path closure would force children to walk along a busy road to reach the primary school.

“The detour needs to be safe and well-lit. We can’t have kids crossing near the works site,” she said.

Marcus said the operator would provide a dedicated school crossing supervisor at the main detour point during drop-off and pick-up times. He said the operator would also send a letter to all parents at the school before the works began.

**Parking restrictions planned**

Residents were told that some on-street parking near the rail bridge would be restricted during the works to allow for construction vehicles. Marcus said the restrictions would be advertised with signs at least one week in advance, and that residents with permits would be able to park in a temporary lot on the other side of the line.

**1. PURPOSE**

This notice is issued by MetroLink Victoria (MLV) to advise stakeholders, local councils, residents, and commuters of a planned maintenance window for the Merri Creek Corridor and associated track infrastructure. The works are scheduled to take place over a five-day period and will require temporary adjustments to train services on the affected lines.

**2. PLANNED MAINTENANCE WINDOW**

The official notice from MetroLink Victoria states that the planned maintenance window runs from 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-20. Record status: current.

This maintenance window has been scheduled to minimise disruption to peak-hour services wherever possible. All works are subject to weather conditions and operational requirements. Should the window need to be adjusted, a supplementary notice will be issued no later than 14 days before the revised commencement date.

**3. SCOPE OF WORKS**

The following activities are planned within the maintenance window:

- Replacement of worn rail sections on the up and down tracks between Westgarth and Merri stations
- Resurfacing of the pedestrian crossing at the Union Lane level crossing (Northcote)
- Upgrade of signalling equipment at the Merri Creek bridge approach
- Vegetation management along the corridor boundary between Merri and Rushall stations
- Inspection and repair of drainage culverts beneath the track formation

Works will be carried out during both daytime and nighttime hours. Night works will be limited to the hours of 22:00 to 05:00 to reduce noise impacts on nearby residents.

Residents and businesses in the vicinity of the works will maintain access to their properties at all times. Pedestrian access across the Merri Creek bridge will be maintained via a temporary walkway. Cyclists are advised to use the alternative route via the shared path on the eastern side of the creek during the works.

Local schools, including Northcote Primary School and Merri Creek Primary School, have been notified of the works and will receive regular updates on any changes to the schedule.

**6. NOISE AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONSIDERATIONS**

MLV is committed to minimising the environmental impact of these works. The following measures will be in place:

- All plant and equipment will meet EPA Victoria noise emission standards
- Dust suppression measures will be used during demolition and excavation works
- Spill kits will be available at all work sites

**17. REVIEW AND UPDATES (continued)**

This notice is issued under the Transport Infrastructure (Maintenance and Operations) Act 2021 and supersedes Maintenance Planning Notice 2025-11 (issued 14/11/2025) for the sections of works described in Sections 3 to 8. Superseded information relating to the original track resurfacing dates in November 2025 is retained in the archive for reference only and should not be used for planning purposes.

MetroLink Victoria reserves the right to alter, postpone, or cancel any of the works described in this notice where operational conditions, weather, or safety requirements demand. Any such change will be communicated via:

- Updated editions of this notice, published on the MetroLink Victoria website
- Electronic message boards at affected stations
- Direct email alerts to subscribers of the Maintenance Works Notification Service

Subscribers can register for email alerts at metrolink.vic.gov.au/works-alerts or by calling 1800 800 007 during business hours.

**18. PROJECT BACKGROUND**

The works described in this notice form part of the Merri Creek Corridor Renewal Program, a broader initiative to upgrade rail infrastructure along the Upfield line between North Melbourne and Coburg. The program commenced in July 2025 and is scheduled for completion in late 2027. The current maintenance window (16/03/2026 to 20/03/2026) addresses identified defects in track geometry, overhead wiring components, and platform infrastructure at stations between Westgarth and Northcote.

These works were identified through routine inspections conducted during the September 2025 track condition assessment. The assessment found that sections of track between Merri and Rushall stations had reached the end of their expected service life and required replacement. Further inspection of overhead wiring equipment at Northcote station identified corrosion in several insulators, which are scheduled for replacement during the wiring inspection on 19/03/2026.

MetroLink Victoria engaged independent consultants to review the condition assessment findings. Their report, completed in October 2025, confirmed the need for the works and recommended that they be carried out as a single coordinated maintenance window to minimise disruption to passengers.

**19. COMMUNITY IMPACT AND MITIGATION MEASURES**

MetroLink Victoria recognises that maintenance works can cause inconvenience to residents, commuters, and local businesses. The following measures have been implemented to reduce impact:

**Noise management**

- All works are scheduled during daytime hours between 09:00 and 15:00, with the exception of the overhead wiring inspection on 19/03/2026 which will commence at 10:00.
- No night works are scheduled. If night works become necessary, a supplementary notice will be issued at least 7 days in advance.
- Contractors will use low-noise equipment wherever practicable, particularly for track grinding activities.
- Noise barriers will be erected along the eastern boundary of the rail corridor between Merri and Rushall stations, adjacent to residential properties on Clarke Street and Union Street.

**Dust and vibration**

- Water carts will be used to suppress dust during track replacement works.
- Vibration monitoring will be conducted at sensitive locations, including the heritage-listed former signal box at Westgarth station. Readings will be reviewed daily, and works will be paused if vibration levels exceed agreed thresholds.

**Access and traffic**

- Pedestrian access to station platforms will be maintained at all times, with temporary ramps provided where step-free access is temporarily affected.
- The car park at Northcote station will be partially closed from 17/03/2026 to 19/03/2026 to allow for equipment staging. Approximately 40 of the usual 120 spaces will remain available.
- Local traffic management plans have been submitted to Darebin City Council and Moreland City Council. No road closures are proposed, but temporary lane restrictions may be in place on Union Street, Westgarth, during deliveries of track materials.

For residents who are unable to attend in person, the presentation materials and a summary of questions raised at each session will be published on the MetroLink Victoria website within five working days of the session. A written summary of the feedback received during the sessions will also be included in the next edition of the project newsletter, scheduled for distribution in late February 2026.

A dedicated project newsletter, titled *Merri Line Maintenance Update*, is distributed to households and businesses within approximately 400 metres of the rail corridor between Merri and Rushall stations. The first edition was distributed in November 2025 and provided an overview of the planned works and the proposed timeline. The second edition is scheduled for distribution in mid-February 2026 and will include:

- a final schedule of works, including any changes made as a result of community feedback;
- details of the temporary car park arrangements at Northcote station;
- a reminder of the contact details for the project team; and
- a list of frequently asked questions.

Residents who do not receive a copy of the newsletter but would like one can request a copy by contacting the project team using the details in Section 22 of this Notice, or by downloading a PDF from the MetroLink Victoria website.

Separate letters have been prepared for sensitive receivers located near the works, including the heritage-listed former signal box at Westgarth station, the aged care facility on Clarke Street, and the childcare centre on Union Street. 1. AUTHORISED WORKS

This permit authorises the Holder to undertake the following activities within the designated work zone at Westgarth Park Level Crossing (hereafter "the Crossing"), located at Merri Creek corridor, Northcote, Victoria:

1.1 Replacement of the existing boom barrier mechanisms and associated control cabling at the Crossing.
1.2 Installation of upgraded track circuit equipment and axle counters adjacent to the Crossing.
1.3 Re-profiling of the approach road pavement within 30 metres of the crossing surface on both sides.
1.4 Removal and replacement of the existing warning signage, including the "Beware of Trains" static signs and the advanced warning signs on the approach roads.
1.5 Testing and commissioning of all new signalling equipment, including interface testing with the MetroLink Victoria train control system.
1.6 Minor earthworks and drainage improvements within the rail corridor boundary, limited to the area between the existing drainage pits and the crossing surface.

2. CLOSURE STATUS

Works Approval Permit W-2210 confirms that the Westgarth Park Level Crossing closure status is closed to road traffic. Record status: current. The closure applies to all road users, including pedestrians and cyclists, except as provided for in Condition 4.3 below. The closure is scheduled to commence at 00:01 on 23/02/2026 and remain in effect continuously until 23:59 on 20/04/2026, or until the authorised works are completed and the Crossing is certified safe for road traffic, whichever occurs first. Any change to this closure period requires a formal variation to this permit under Condition 9.

3. VALIDITY PERIOD

3.1 This permit is valid from 16/02/2026 until 30/04/2026 inclusive.
3.2 Works may only be undertaken during the validity period. Any works not completed by the expiry date must cease, and the Holder must apply for a new permit or a variation to this permit.
3.3 The permit lapses immediately if the Holder ceases to hold the relevant public liability insurance required under Condition 5.4.
3.4 No works are authorised outside the validity period, including any preparatory or reinstatement works, unless explicitly covered by another approval.

4. CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL

4.1 All works must be carried out in accordance with the approved drawings and specifications listed in Schedule A of this permit and the accompanying Works Method Statement (WMS) dated 28/01/2026, revision 3.
4.2 The Holder must maintain a safe work zone at all times. This includes the provision of temporary fencing, warning lights, and signage in accordance with the Road Management Act 2004 (Vic) and the relevant Australian Standards.
4.3 Pedestrian access across the Crossing will be maintained via a temporary footbridge adjacent to the site, to be installed by 20/02/2026 and available for use for the duration of the closure. The footbridge is not part of the authorised works but is a condition of the closure approval.
4.4 The Holder must provide a minimum of 14 days' written notice to the Merri-bek City Council, Victoria Police, and the Department of Transport and Planning prior to the commencement of the road closure.
4.5 Works must not obstruct the Merri Creek shared path unless a separate temporary path diversion is provided and approved by Council.
4.6 No works are permitted on public holidays, including Australia Day (26/01/2026) and the Easter period (Good Friday 03/04/2026 to Easter Monday 06/04/2026 inclusive), unless prior written approval is obtained from MetroLink Victoria.
4.7 Works on the rail corridor are restricted to the approved track possession windows. The Holder must coordinate with the MetroLink Victoria Network Access Coordinator for all track possession bookings.
4.8 The Holder must undertake a pre-works dilapidation survey of the adjacent properties and the crossing surface, and provide a copy to MetroLink Victoria within 7 days of the commencement of works.
4.9 All personnel engaged in works on the rail corridor must hold current rail safety worker accreditation and be inducted to the site.

documents.content:
**Hobsons Bay Weekly**
**Community Concerns Over Rail Works**
**Published 15/01/2026**

Residents across the Altona North and Seabrook area are voicing concerns ahead of the scheduled rail maintenance works along the Williamstown and Werribee lines, with many worried about noise, dust, and the disruption to local traffic during the multi-week program.

The works, which are due to begin in late February and run through to mid-March, will involve track resurfacing, signal upgrades, and the replacement of sleepers on a number of sections. While the operator has described the program as "essential maintenance" that will improve reliability, local residents are not convinced the timing or the communication has been adequate.

"We only got a letter in the mail last week," said Margaret Chen, a Seabrook resident whose backyard backs onto the rail corridor. "It said there would be night works and that we should expect some noise. But it didn't say how many nights or how loud it would be. My grandson is a shift worker, he needs to sleep during the day. This is going to be a real problem."

The Hobsons Bay Weekly archive shows the published article date as 2026-01-15. Record status: historical. The article is based on interviews conducted over the past week with residents, local business owners, and a spokesperson for the rail operator.

Concerns raised at a community drop-in session held at the Altona North Community Centre on Tuesday evening included:

- The potential for increased dust from grinding works, particularly on dry days.
- Uncertainty about the exact dates and times of the loudest activities.
- The impact on local bus replacement services, with residents worried about longer commute times.
- Whether the operator would provide any compensation for residents who may be significantly affected.

John Petrovski, who runs a small mechanics workshop on Millers Road, said the works could not have come at a worse time. "We're coming into our busiest period," he said. "If the road is blocked or the traffic is backed up, people aren't going to want to come down here to drop off their cars. I've already had two customers ask if we're going to be open. It's a worry."

The rail operator has stated that a "comprehensive community engagement plan" was in place, including letterbox drops, social media updates, and a dedicated hotline. However, several residents told the Weekly that they had not recieved the promised information until very recently.

"I checked their website last week and there was nothing about the dates," said David O'Leary, a commuter who uses the Werribee line daily. "Then suddenly, the letter arrives and it's all happening in a month. It doesn't feel like they're listening to us."

One point of confusion for some residents is the distinction between the major works and routine maintenance. A fact sheet distributed at the community session described the program as "routine renewal works," but also mentioned "significant night-time possessions" on certain weekends. Residents said the language was confusing and that they were unsure which activities would affect them.

"I asked the person at the session if the grinding would be happening right outside my place, and they couldn't tell me," said Mrs Chen. "They said it would depend on the final schedule. Well, when will the final schedule be known? We need to plan our lives."

The operator has said that a detailed schedule, including a map of affected sections, will be published on its website by the end of January. A spokesperson said that "every effort" would be made to keep residents informed of any changes.

Local councillor Sarah Nguyen, who attended the community session, said she would be writing to the operator to request a more detailed breakdown of the works and a clear timeline for when residents could expect to receive information.

"I understand that maintenance is necessary, but the communication has been patchy," Cr Nguyen said. "My office has received several calls from residents who are anxious about what's coming. We need clarity, not just a general overview."

**Noise a Key Worry as Rail Works Near, Residents Say**

By Maria Delgado, Hobsons Bay Weekly

15 January 2026

The sound of grinding steel, the rumble of machinery, the warning beeps of reversing trucks – for residents living closest to the Werribee line, the question of noise is becoming one of the biggest concerns about the upcoming maintenance program.

At last week's community session at the Altona North Community Centre, noise was the issue raised most often, according to organisers. Several people who live within a few hundred metres of the tracks said they were worried about sleepless nights and the impact on young children and elderly relatives.

One resident, who asked not to be named, said she had taken her own measurements using a phone app during a recent test run of machinery in the area.

"I stood in my backyard and the app said it was going up to 65 dB(A) decibels," she said. "I don't know how accurate the app is, but it was loud enough that I had to raise my voice to speak to my neighbour. If that's what it's like during the day, what's it going to be like at two in the morning?"

The reading has not been independently verified, and the resident acknowledged that a phone app is not a professional sound meter. However, her experience reflects a broader anxiety among residents that the operator has not been upfront about the level of disruption.

Hobsons Bay Weekly reported noise level 65 dB(A) decibels. Record status: pending verification. The figure has been shared on a local Facebook group, where it has generated dozens of comments from people asking whether the works will meet legal noise limits.

Altona North resident Peter Mifsud said he had lived near the line for 22 years and was used to the occasional train passing. "But this is different. This is industrial. I've got a workshop at the back of my place and I can tell you, the noise from the test runs carried right across the yard."

Mr Mifsud said he had not been contacted by the operator directly, despite living close enough to the tracks to see the overhead wires from his kitchen window. "I got a letter last week, but it was a generic thing. It didn't say anything about noise. It just said there would be works and gave a hotline number. I called the hotline and the person on the other end couldn't tell me anything about noise levels either. They said it would be 'managed'."

A spokesperson for the rail operator said that noise management was a key part of the planning process. "We are committed to minimising disruption for residents. All works will be carried out in accordance with relevant environmental guidelines, and we will have noise monitoring in place at key locations. We encourage residents to contact our hotline if they have specific concerns."

The spokesperson did not provide details of what those guidelines are, or what the monitoring would involve. When asked about the 65 dB(A) reading, the spokesperson said the operator could not comment on unverified measurements taken by members of the public.

Cr Sarah Nguyen, who has been liaising with residents since the community session, said she had written to the operator requesting a clear statement on expected noise levels.

"I've asked them to publish the predicted noise levels for each section of the works, and to tell us what mitigations will be in place. At the moment, residents are being asked to take the operator's word for it that everything will be fine. That's not good enough."

Cr Nguyen said she had also asked about the possibility of noise barriers or temporary screens, particularly near the Altona North and Brooklyn sections of the line. "I haven't had a detailed response yet. I'll be following up next week."

Some residents have also raised concerns about the timing of the works. The operator has said that some weekend possessions will involve night-time work, but has not yet published the full schedule. Residents say they need to know well in advance so they can make arrangements, particularly those who work night shifts or have young children.

**Hobsons Bay Weekly**
**Community Concerns Over Rail Works**
*By Liam O’Connor, local affairs reporter*
*Published 15 January 2026*

---

**Residents demand answers as community meeting hears of vibration, dust and access worries**

More than 60 residents packed the Altona North Community Centre on Tuesday night (10 February) for a follow-up meeting on the upcoming rail maintenance works, with many saying they still feel in the dark about what the multi-week project will mean for their daily lives.

The meeting, organised by Cr Sarah Nguyen and the Altona North Residents Association, was the second community session held since the operator first announced the works in late December. While the operator sent two representatives to the earlier session in January, Tuesday night’s meeting was attended by a single project officer, who was not authorised to speak on the record about specific noise or vibration predictions.

“I understand people are frustrated. I’m here to listen and to take your questions back to the project team,” said the officer, who introduced himself only as Marcus. He said a full project update would be published on the operator’s website “in the coming weeks”.

That response did little to satisfy those in the room. Several residents spoke of ongoing uncertainty about the scope of the works, the duration of track closures, and what they described as a lack of clear communication from the rail operator.

**Vibration concerns near Merri Creek**

One of the most detailed presentations came from a resident of the Brooklyn area, who said she had been monitoring vibration levels in her home using a mobile phone app.

“I’m not a scientist, but I know my house shakes when a freight train goes past. If they’re going to be doing grinding and tamping work right near the creek, I want to know what that’s going to do to my foundations,” she said.

Marcus said the operator would be carrying out vibration monitoring at “a small number of sensitive locations” but could not confirm whether those locations included any private residences. He said the monitoring would be in place “before and during” the works, and that residents would be notified if any readings exceeded guidelines.

Residents asked for the monitoring locations to be published, but Marcus said that information was “commercial in confidence”.

**Dust and air quality concerns raised**

Several residents also raised concerns about dust from ballast replacement and track grinding, particularly in the warmer months. One parent from the Altona North estate said she was worried about her son, who has asthma.

“Last time there were works near the line, we had dust on our windowsills for weeks. I don’t want to be told it’s safe when no one has actually measured anything,” she said.

Marcus said the operator would be using water carts to suppress dust during works and that an air quality monitor would be installed at a fixed location near the Altona North shops. He did not provide a timeline for when the monitor would be installed, or how the data would be made public.

Cr Nguyen, who chaired the meeting, said she would write to the operator again to request that air quality data be published on a weekly basis.

“That seems like a reasonable thing to ask. If they’re measuring it, why can’t we see the results?” she said.

**Access to the shared path**

A recurring theme was the impact of the works on the shared walking and cycling path that runs alongside the rail corridor. Residents said the path was a key connection for people commuting to the Altona North business park and for school children walking to the local primary school.

Marcus said the path would be closed in sections during the works, with detours in place. He said the operator would publish a “path closure map” on its website at least two weeks before each section closed, but he could not say when the first closure would begin.

One resident, who said she uses the path daily to cycle to work, said a two-week notice period was not enough.

**Community Concerns Over Rail Works**

**Council promises weekly dust data after public meeting**

By Elena Marsh, Hobsons Bay Weekly
15 January 2026

The operator behind the upcoming rail maintenance works will face a community reference group, after a packed meeting at the Altona North Community Centre on Wednesday night heard repeated concerns about dust, noise, and a lack of detail.

About 80 residents attended the meeting, which was chaired by Cr Linh Nguyen and organised by the Hobsons Bay City Council. The operator’s community liaison officer, David Marcus, took questions for close to two hours.

The meeting came as the operator confirmed that the main maintenance window will run from Saturday 21 February to Sunday 8 March 2026. During that time, buses will replace trains on the Williamstown and Werribee lines between Newport and Laverton.

**Bus replacement confirmed**

Marcus confirmed that a bus replacement service will run throughout the maintenance window, with buses stopping at all stations on the affected section. He said the service will run every 10 minutes during peak times and every 20 minutes off-peak.

“We know this will be an inconvenience, and we are asking people to allow extra travel time,” he said.

Several residents asked whether the bus service would be able to cope with demand, particularly during the morning peak. Marcus said additional buses would be held at Newport station as a backup, but he could not confirm how many.

One resident asked whether the Route 671 bus, which connects Altona North to Newport, would be affected. Marcus said that route was not part of the replacement service, but that the operator was in discussions with the bus operator about possible timetable changes.

“We are aware that local bus services will also be busier, and we are working with the operator to monitor that,” he said.

**Community reference group to be formed**

Cr Nguyen announced that the council would establish a community reference group to meet with the operator weekly during the works. The group would include representatives from residents’ groups, the Altona North business park, and the local primary school.

“We have heard tonight that people want more than a website update. They want a regular, face-to-face conversation,” she said.

Marcus said the operator would support the group and would send a senior project manager to each meeting. He said the first meeting would be held in the week beginning 9 February, with details to be published on the operator’s website.

**Questions remain over monitoring**

Despite the commitments, several questions remained unanswered at the end of the meeting. Residents asked for the following information to be published before the works begin:

- The exact locations of the vibration monitoring equipment, which Marcus had earlier said would be “commercial in confidence”.
- The timeline for installation of the air quality monitor near the Altona North shops.
- A map of the shared path closures, which Marcus said would be published at least two weeks before each section closed.
- The criteria for stopping works if dust or vibration readings exceeded guidelines.

Cr Nguyen said she would write to the operator again to request the information, and would ask that the responses be published on the council’s website.

**School drop-off concerns**

Parents at the meeting raised concerns about the impact of the works on school drop-off and pick-up times. One mother said the shared path closure would force children to walk along a busy road to reach the primary school.

“The detour needs to be safe and well-lit. We can’t have kids crossing near the works site,” she said.

Marcus said the operator would provide a dedicated school crossing supervisor at the main detour point during drop-off and pick-up times. He said the operator would also send a letter to all parents at the school before the works began.

**Parking restrictions planned**

Residents were told that some on-street parking near the rail bridge would be restricted during the works to allow for construction vehicles. Marcus said the restrictions would be advertised with signs at least one week in advance, and that residents with permits would be able to park in a temporary lot on the other side of the line.
